mappings.note: Judicial review as the court testing laws and government action against the Constitution. Goal-level CG-SST3 for an institution of Indian democracy; the frame has no judiciary LO.
Why a state needs a permanent population - shared culture and identification with the territory. Goal-level CG-SST3 for the concept of the state.
Sovereignty as internal control without external interference. Goal-level CG-SST3, matching the other sovereignty items.
The police maintaining order and public safety on the state's behalf. Goal-level CG-SST3 for an organ of the state; LO-115 is rejected because no citizen dealing with an office is described.
The legislature representing the people and making law that binds everyone. Goal-level CG-SST3; LO-110 is rejected because the question is about the body's function, not how members are elected.
Republic against monarchy - elected versus inherited head of state. Goal-level CG-SST3 for forms of state.
Why India is both democratic and a republic. Goal-level CG-SST3 for the character of the Indian state.
'Dominance of the majority' as pursuing majority interest at the cost of minority rights. LO-106, the significance of equality in a democracy.
The Constitution limiting power so leaders cannot violate basic rights. LO-106 for equal protection, CG-SST3 for the constitutional machinery that delivers it.
The permanent executive advising, implementing and keeping administration running through political change. LO-115, the functioning of government offices.

Elected ministers on fixed terms against career bureaucrats serving to retirement. Goal-level CG-SST3 for the institutional distinction; LO-115 is reserved for items about what those offices actually do.
C.B. Muthamma as the first woman in the Indian Foreign Service and her fight against gender-biased service rules. LO-112 exactly.
Government as protector, provider and regulator. Goal-level CG-SST3 for the roles of the state; no LO covers them.
RTI letting citizens demand records of government action and spending. LO-115, holding a government office to account.
Civil society organisations raising awareness and pressing government on public concerns. CG-SST3 for their place in a democracy, LO-108 for the local issues they take up.
Silent Valley: public pressure cancelling the dam and producing a National Park. LO-100 for the forest conserved, LO-108 for citizens acting on a public issue.
The judiciary upholding the rule of law, settling disputes and checking unfair government action. Goal-level CG-SST3.
Why India decentralised - size and diversity needing national, State and local tiers. LO-109 exactly.
The third tier created to let citizens solve immediate community problems. LO-109, local against State government.
Gram Swaraj - self-sufficient villages, interdependent for the rest. LO-109, matching the other Gandhi item.
Defence and foreign affairs as Union subjects. Allocation between tiers, LO-109.
Streetlamps, drainage and parks as local-government business. LO-109 exactly.
Decentralisation improving accountability by putting leaders within reach of the people. LO-109; CG-SST3 is not added because the argument is specifically about the local tier.
Print, electronic and social media as platforms for citizens to press government. LO-113, the role of media in a democracy.

Tribal land protected in law, unbuyable without community consent. LO-108, interpreting a rights issue in a region; CG-SST3 is not added because the answer stays on the community's position rather than the organ enforcing it.
State and government distinguished through the school analogy. Goal-level CG-SST3.
Why sovereignty is essential to a state. Goal-level CG-SST3.
Legislature making law, executive implementing it, and why the separation matters. Goal-level CG-SST3 for the organs of government.
How a republic's constitutional limits stop the majority overriding minority rights. LO-106, the significance of equality in a democracy.
The significance of Muthamma's legal struggle for gender equality. LO-112 exactly. (Empty answer on this row; see report.)
The same Muthamma question with its answer run into the stem: denied promotion, she took the Ministry to the Supreme Court, which struck the rules down. LO-112. (Merged stem; see report.)
RTI used to expose negligence and force officials to act. LO-115, accountability of a government office.
Civil society mobilising opinion and changing policy, with Silent Valley as the instance. CG-SST3 for their democratic role, LO-108 for the public issue contested.
Why an independent judiciary is vital - a neutral watchdog over political power. Goal-level CG-SST3.
The rationale for devolving power to local government in a country of India's size. LO-109 exactly. (Answer breaks off at a watermark and resumes mid-sentence on another topic; see report.)

Bagepalli case study: an RTI application forcing officials to fix dangerous roadwork, illustrating transparency and accountability. LO-115 for the office held to account, LO-108 for acting on an issue in one's own region.
Silent Valley case study naming civil society and asking why its intervention mattered. LO-100 for the forest, LO-108 for citizens acting on a public issue.
Case study resolving broken streetlamps and drains to the Gram Panchayat, and naming the principle decentralisation. LO-109 exactly.
Case study on the Dongria Kondh blocking a mining corporation. LO-108 for the rights issue in a region, CG-SST3 for part (b), which asks which organ enforces the protective law.

Education handled across tiers - legislatures passing the Right to Education, the political executive designing Samagra Shiksha, the permanent executive delivering it at block level. LO-109 for the tiers, LO-115 for the offices that implement.

Matsya nyaya in the Arthashastra - the big fish eating the small where there is no law. CG-SST3 for the case it makes for ordered government, CG-SST2 because the argument is drawn from an ancient text.
Government as provider - roads, hospitals, welfare, food safety, free schooling. CG-SST3 for the role, LO-115 for the offices through which those services reach people.
Political and permanent executives compared on selection, tenure and function. Goal-level CG-SST3 for the institutional distinction.
Washington's refusal of a crown and what it settled about republican government. Goal-level CG-SST3; the chapter uses it to make a constitutional point, not to teach history, so CG-SST2 is rejected.
The police as the state's enforcement agent, using force within constitutional limits. Goal-level CG-SST3 for an organ of the state.
A Resident Welfare Association's majority vote harming one vulnerable resident until the rule was amended. LO-106 - the clearest illustration in the chapter of why equality constrains majority rule.
